title: D-FINE-L vs RT-DETR-R101: same-protocol benchmark
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol: D-FINE-L leads by 3.2 mAP points with fewer than half the parameters, and beats RT-DETR-R101 on most runtimes.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: D-FINE-L is the more accurate model: 60.0 vs 56.8 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R101 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, and it reaches that with fewer parameters (31.24M vs 76.56M) and about half the VRAM (245 vs 456 MB). RT-DETR-R101 is 7.3% faster in PyTorch (23.6 vs 21.9 FPS), but D-FINE-L is faster on ONNX, TensorRT FP32, and Jetson. Pick by runtime.

D-FINE-L (31.24M parameters, Apache-2.0) and RT-DETR-R101 (76.56M, Apache-2.0) both evaluate at 640 px input, so the input resolution matches and does not skew the comparison. D-FINE-L is less than half the size here. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, A100, and Jetson Orin, so this comparison covers the deploy targets where the answer changes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. D-FINE-L and RT-DETR-R101 highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. D-FINE-L measures 60.0 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R101's 56.8, a 3.2 point lead. The gap is wider on small objects: 45.9 vs 39.2 mAP_small, a 17.2% relative difference. D-FINE-L reaches that with fewer than half the parameters.

RT-DETR-R101 leads in PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti: 23.6 vs 21.9 FPS, a 7.3% edge. That edge does not survive most conversions. On ONNX Runtime D-FINE-L runs 50.9 to RT-DETR-R101's 47.5 FPS; on TensorRT FP32, 72.3 to 64.4.

The PyTorch speed result does not generalize. D-FINE-L is faster on ONNX Runtime, TensorRT FP32, and Jetson Orin (4.7 vs 2.8 FPS). RT-DETR-R101 keeps its edge on TensorRT FP16: 88.0 vs 69.3 FPS. Pick the runtime you deploy on, then read that row.

Pick D-FINE-L for nearly every deployment: it is more accurate at every object size, uses about half the VRAM, and is faster on ONNX, TensorRT FP32, and Jetson. Pick RT-DETR-R101 only where its PyTorch or TensorRT FP16 throughput matters. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

dfine = LibreYOLO("LibreDFINEl.pt")      # 31.24M params, 60.0 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr101.pt") # 76.56M params, 56.8 mAP@50-95

results = dfine("image.jpg")
